text:
Anya: Quick question — the inline threshold rows have a 'ghost' placeholder row when you open the suppression preview. Users are reading it as an actionable row, not a preview. Thoughts? :thinking: Jordan: I noticed that too in usability tests. It looks like a real row because it has the same affordances (hover, kebab menu). Maybe make preview rows visually distinct and non-interactive? :eyes: Kevin: Agree. Two quick options: 1) make preview rows have dashed outline + reduced opacity + pointer-events: none, 2) move preview to an isolated panel above the table. My vote is #1 for density reasons. Emily: If we go with pointer-events: none we need to make sure keyboard users can still get the context. For a11y we should expose the preview via aria-live or a dedicated readout region. Anya: Good call. Jordan — can you mock up a sample with dashed row style + small "preview" badge? Also copy change: current preview label says "Preview: suppression" which feels clunky. Maybe "Suppression preview" or "How suppression will apply"? Jordan: Will do. Quick mock notes: - dashed 1px #d6d9dd - 0.7 opacity - small pill (label) at row start "Preview" - tooltip on hover that says "This row shows how the threshold will look if suppression is applied" Kevin: For copy, "Suppression preview" reads fine. "How suppression will apply" is clearer for non-technical PMs. Leaning to clarity over brevity here. Emily: Also need to think about screen readers: when preview toggles on, we should announce "Suppression preview shown for X channels". Proposed aria: `aria-live="polite"` container that updates to "Preview: [short summary]". Example: "Suppression preview active: will mute alerts to Slack and Email for 1 hour". Anya: Nice. Also small keyboard flow nit: when preview is enabled and focus is inside the thresholds table, hitting Tab should skip to the preview summary, not land on ghost-row buttons (which are non-interactive). Otherwise it traps keyboard users. Jordan: Implementation note: set tabindex="-1" on the ghost elements and programmatically focus the summary element when preview opens. Add a focus ring style for the summary so keyboard users have visual context. DesignBot: I generated a quick aria snippet for the summary box to paste into the prototype: ```
Suppression preview active: mutes alerts to Slack, Email for 1 hour.
``` Anya: That looks good. One more copy quibble: the suppression pill currently says "Muted" after you confirm — product wants it to read "Suppressed" to match backend naming. Which do we pick? PM asked for "Suppressed" but designers prefer "Muted" as it's friendlier. Kevin: Product consistency vs user clarity. If backend tooling and audit logs show "Suppressed" we should show both places: UI copy friendly ("Muted until 2:00 PM") + secondary microcopy or tooltip "(status: Suppressed)" for engineers. Emily: +1. Also accessibility concern: tooltip content must be keyboard accessible and read by screenreader on focus. Use aria-describedby linking from the pill to the tooltip element. Jordan: I'll update the mock: dashed preview rows, preview pill reads "Suppression preview", confirmed state pill shows "Muted until 2:00 PM" with `aria-describedby` pointing to a hidden description that contains "status: suppressed". Anya: Perfect. Can you also include a test case for users with multiple suppressed thresholds so the summary text doesn't become too long? Example truncation: "Suppression preview active: mutes alerts to Slack, Email, PagerDuty..." — we should ellipsize and provide a "+2 more" link that expands full list. Jordan: Noted. UX pattern: inline ellipsis with a button "+N more" that toggles a small popover listing channels. Ensure popover is accessible (role="dialog", focus trap). DesignBot: Mock link: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/suppression-preview—will attach updated frames after changes. Kevin: One last tiny thing: color contrast on the preview dashed bg at 0.7 opacity + grey text might drop below AA. Please run contrast check. If it fails, use a slightly darker stroke or stronger badge color. Anya: Thanks all. Action items: Jordan — update mock and include focus flow + popover behavior. Emily — write a short a11y acceptance criteria (aria-live message, focus movement, tooltip-describedby). Kevin — check contrast and confirm hex values. I'll sync with PM on "Muted" vs "Suppressed" final copy. :thumbsup:
